The animal with distinctive black and white stripes is the zebra.

Regarding the assumptions in the projectile motion problem, there is a logical contradiction that violates mathematical and physical principles. The statement claims that "the initial velocity is known and remains constant until the projectile leaves the launching device." This is incorrect. In physics and mathematics, velocity is a vector quantity that changes if there is acceleration. During the launching phase, the projectile accelerates from rest (or a lower speed) to its initial launch velocity. Therefore, the velocity is not constant during the launch; it is changing. The assumption of constant velocity only applies to the horizontal component of motion *after* the projectile has left the launcher and air resistance is neglected, but even then, the vertical component changes due to gravity. The statement conflates the state of the projectile while it is still in the launcher with the idealized conditions of free flight.
